value: Anne has a pale complexion.

She has big, solemn gray eyes, which are starrier than those of other girls, as well as delicate features. Though her hair is naturally red and often worn in long braids, it at times streams unbraided in a torrent of brightness, clusters in short silky curls, turns green after an incident, or lightens to auburn. Over time, her height increases until she is taller than Marilla.

label: Personality
value: Anne has an exceptionally vivid imagination.
unit: Characterized by an exceptionally vivid imagination, she frequently falls into daydreams and expresses herself in a talkative manner. This imaginative temperament contributes to an impulsive nature, where actions and words are executed without prior reflection. She possesses an intense emotional capacity, displaying passionate affection alongside a stubborn tenacity for holding grudges and a quick temper. Despite this fiery disposition, she is generous and demonstrates practical abilities, including rapid running speed, a talented singing voice, and a talent for writing compositions. She has also shown remarkable skill and composure when treating a sick child suffering from croup. Driven by strong ambitions, she aspires to excel academically, aiming to become a teacher, win a scholarship, and attend college, while harboring a specific fear of traversing the Haunted Wood after dark.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early childhood as an orphan, being shuffled between foster families—where she helped care for many children—and an overcrowded asylum in Hopeton. She was eventually adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, though her initial arrival was met with surprise because they had requested a boy. Anne rapidly made Green Gables her home, swearing a deep friendship with Diana Barry and establishing a fierce academic rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he rudely called her 'Carrots.' Over her early years in Avonlea, Anne got into frequent scrapes, such as accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine, accidentally flavoring a cake with liniment for the new minister, and dyeing her hair green. Despite these mishaps, she proved her resourcefulness by nursing Diana's sister through croup, winning over Diana's formidable Aunt Josephine, and excelling under the tutelage of her teacher, Miss Stacy. Her hard work culminated in tying for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's Academy, where she subsequently won the prestigious Avery scholarship. However, following Matthew's sudden death from shock over a bank failure and Marilla's diagnosis of failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables. She chose to teach locally instead, happily reconciling her long-standing rivalry with Gilbert after he gave up the Avonlea school position for her.

unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early childhood as an orphan, being shuffled between foster families—where she helped care for many children—and an overcrowded asylum in Hopeton. She was eventually adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, though her initial arrival was met with surprise because they had requested a boy. Anne rapidly made Green Gables her home, swearing a deep friendship with Diana Barry and establishing a fierce academic rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe after he rudely called her 'Carrots.' Over her early years in Avonlea, Anne got into frequent scrapes, such as accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine, accidentally flavoring a cake with liniment for the new minister, and dyeing her hair green. Despite these mishaps, she proved her resourcefulness by nursing Diana's sister through croup, winning over Diana's formidable Aunt Josephine, and excelling under the tutelage of her teacher, Miss Stacy. Her hard work culminated in tying for first place on the entrance exams for Queen's Academy, where she subsequently won the prestigious Avery scholarship. However, following Matthew's sudden death from shock over a bank failure and Marilla's diagnosis of failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables. She chose to teach locally instead, happily reconciling her long-standing rivalry with Gilbert after he gave up the Avonlea school position for her.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn’t you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I’m here? Oh, do let me!"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta.
unit: After spending three years in Alberta with his ill father and a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick, Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea. On his first day back at school, he pulled Anne Shirley's braid and called her 'Carrots,' receiving a smashed slate over his head for the insult; despite his contrite apology, she refused to forgive him, initiating an intense academic rivalry between them. Months later, Gilbert rescued Anne from a leaky boat at a bridge pile and offered his friendship, but she rejected him once more. The two continued their fierce academic competition through Queen's Academy, where Gilbert ultimately won the medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that Anne intended to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla, Gilbert selflessly gave up his position as the Avonlea schoolteacher so she could take the job, prompting the pair to finally forgive their past feud and become close friends.

Months later, Gilbert rescued Anne from a leaky boat at a bridge pile and offered his friendship, but she rejected him once more. The two continued their fierce academic competition through Queen's Academy, where Gilbert ultimately won the medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that Anne intended to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla, Gilbert selflessly gave up his position as the Avonlea schoolteacher so she could take the job, prompting the pair to finally forgive their past feud and become close friends.

label: History
value: Josephine Barry was rich.
unit: Josephine Barry was a rich, seventy-year-old aunt of Mr. Barry who lived at Beechwood in Charlottetown. During a visit to Avonlea, she was infuriated when Anne Shirley and Diana leaped into her spare-room bed, but she forgave the girls and remained in town after Anne delivered a sincere, imaginative apology that amused her and struck up a friendship. She later hosted Anne and Diana at her Charlottetown home during the Exhibition, realizing how much she enjoyed Anne's lively company.

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "but I guess she didn’t make much of a mistake after all. If I’d a child like Anne in the house all the time I’d be a better and happier woman."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

value: Marilla Cuthbert is self-contained.

Additionally, she possesses the skill to make celebrated three-year-old homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert suffered from a painful remark.
unit: In her childhood, Marilla Cuthbert suffered from a painful remark made by an aunt about her plain appearance. In her youth, she had been sweethearts with John Blythe, but their relationship ended after she refused to forgive him following a quarrel. Marilla led an easy life at Green Gables until she and her brother, Matthew, arranged to adopt an orphan boy. Shocked when Matthew brought home an orphan girl named Anne instead, Marilla initially insisted on returning her, but changed her mind after hearing Anne's tragic background and learning that a harsh local woman wanted her. Adopting Anne, Marilla took on her religious and daily upbringing. Over time, Marilla grew deeply fond of Anne despite her frequent mishaps, such as accidentally serving currant wine to Diana Barry or accidentally dyeing her hair green. When Anne fell from a roof, Marilla realized how much she truly loved her. Marilla supported Anne's education, allowing her to take advanced classes and attend Queen's Academy. Following Matthew's sudden death and news of her own failing eyesight, Marilla considered selling Green Gables, but Anne gave up her college scholarship to remain home and care for her.

Known for being farseeing and skilled at sewing, she never shirks her share of work. However, she is an outspoken, officious, and meddlesome person who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, often nagging people to do right and remaining easily shocked by any naughtiness. Though she possesses a critical and fault-finding eye, she ultimately has a kindly heart and is considered one of the kindest souls in her community.

unit: After finishing school, Anne attends Entrance examinations in town, staying with Aunt Josephine. Anne shares the triumphant news with Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde before ending her evening with Mrs. Allan.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: Anne and Diana walk to school, discussing their scenic route, local school gossip, and the return of Gilbert Blythe. In the classroom, Gilbert pulls Anne's braid and calls her 'Carrots,' prompting Anne to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand in front of the class, and despite Gilbert's contrite apology afterward, Anne refuses to forgive him.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
value: Matthew realizes that Anne's plain clothes set her apart from other girls.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
unit: Matthew realizes that Anne's plain clothes set her apart from other girls, so he decides to buy her a fashionable dress for Christmas. After an awkward attempt to shop at Lawson's store, he gets Mrs. Rachel Lynde to buy and sew a brown dress with puffed sleeves for her. On Christmas morning, Anne is overjoyed to receive the dress from Matthew, along with slippers sent by Aunt Josephine, and she goes on to star in the successful evening concert.

unit: Anne and Diana walk to school, discussing their scenic route, local school gossip, and the return of Gilbert Blythe. Mrs. Lynde reveals that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so Anne could have it, leading Anne and Gilbert to finally reconcile their rivalry and become good friends.
